item.title: FBI arrests a woman accused of spying on Taiwan leader's family for China
item.description: The FBI and U.S. prosecutors say Wanying Zhang, also know as Heather, surveilled the Taiwanese president's son and his family.

item.title: People are asking ChatGPT to help them decide how to vote in the midterms
item.description: Voters are already voting in the midterms. This year, some voters are trying something new to get ready for the election: asking AI to help research their ballot and even decide who to vote for.

item.title: Sexual assault survivors share stories online following Cornell rape allegations
item.description: Hearing about the sexual assault of a Cornell University student in 2024 is bringing back memories for people who have experienced abuse. With the story everywhere, it's hard to ignore.

item.title: The USDA's largest and oldest lab is set to close
item.description: The USDA's flagship agricultural research lab could close this week. Scientists warn that could hurt U.S. food supply.

item.title: In 'Ply,' Hernán Díaz imagines what we become after the world we know
item.description: Pulitzer prize winner Hernán Díaz' new book 'Ply' follows a young woman who siphons electricity to power punk shows in a re-wilded world. Díaz tells NPR how the novel came to examine selfhood, identity and intimacy.

item.title: Supreme Court starts a new term with a case about who pays for climate damage
item.description: The Supreme Court starts its new term with a Colorado county's claim that an oil refinery worsened climate change. The ruling could determine whether similar cases can move forward.

item.title: How much are AI data centers adding to your electricity bill?
item.description: Americans are worried AI data centers will raise their electricity bills. Congress has come up with a plan to protect ratepayers, but there's no easy way to find out what AI is costing them.
